judged_text: Lark createEvent uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` regardless of which credential is creating, so member credentials address the main host's Lark calendar ID instead of their own destination. Collective bookings with multiple Lark hosts either fail per-member (no access to the main host's calendar, error swallowed) or, if the calendar is shared, create duplicate events on the main host's calendar instead of one event per host.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Lark createEvent uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` regardless of which credential is creating, so member credentials address the main host's Lark calendar ID instead of their own destination. Collective bookings with multiple Lark hosts either fail per-member (no access to the main host's calendar, error swallowed) or, if the calendar is shared, create duplicate events on the main host's calendar instead of one event per host.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` (and related methods) now derive the calendar ID from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`, i.e. always the first destination calendar in the array. Meanwhile the diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination calendar to create per-destination events, but it passes the same `event` object each time (it does not swap/target the current destination). Unlike Google, Lark does not accept/use a `credentialId` to pick the matching destination calendar. Therefore, for collective bookings with multiple Lark hosts (multiple destination calendars in the array), Lark event creation will target `destinationCalendar[0]` (main host) regardless of which credential is being used, causing failures or duplicate events on the main host calendar as described.
